requirements.text: Clicking search button shall search the text entered in URLBar.
Starting a URL bar search shall display the search results in the sidebar search tab.
It shall be possible to start a search from within the sidebar search tab.
A user shall be able to change the search engine.
A conducted search shall be bookmarked.

reference_cases.title: TC-135
reference_cases.description:
INITIAL CONDITIONS
Open a new browser window.

STEPS/DESCRIPTION
1. Type something into the URL Bar or edit already existing contents.
2. Click the "Search" button to the right of the URL Bar.

EXPECTED RESULTS
1. Clicking the "Search" button with a "dirty" URL bar should launch a search on the terms in the URL bar.
2. You should see a page with search results in the browser content window. *there are MySidebar ramifications with this testcase that are treated elsewhere.

reference_cases.title: TC-136
reference_cases.description:
INITIAL CONDITIONS
1. Open a new browser window.
2. All prefs should be set to their defaults (new profile).

STEPS/DESCRIPTION
1. Type a multi-word search term in the URL bar. Anything will do, "Claudius 'CMaximus' Gayle" for example.
2. Click the "Search" Button.

EXPECTED RESULTS
1. After search results load in the browser window, the Sidebar should pop open to the Search tab and be populated with search results as well.
2. The textfield in the sidebar search tab should be populated with your search term exactly as you typed it.

reference_cases.title: TC-137
reference_cases.description:
INITIAL CONDITIONS
1. Open a new browser window.
2. All prefs should be set to their defaults (new profile).

STEPS/DESCRIPTION
1. Open the Sidebar to the Search tab.
2. Type a search term into the textbox. Anything will do, "CMaximus" for example.
3. Click the "Search" Button next to the textfield.

EXPECTED RESULTS
1. Search results from the default search engine should load in the browser window.
2. Results should load in the Search tab as well.
3. Search results in the search tab should be prefixed by an icon representing the search engine - for each result.

reference_cases.title: TC-138
reference_cases.description:
INITIAL CONDITIONS
1. Open a new browser window.
2. All prefs should be set to their defaults (new profile).

STEPS/DESCRIPTION
1. Run the single-search test first.
2. In the dropdown box after the word "using" select a different search engine.
3. Click the "Search" Button next to the textfield.
4. Repeat steps 2-3 as desired.

EXPECTED RESULTS
1. Search results from the chosen search engine should load in the browser window.
2. Results should load in the Search tab as well.
3. Search results in the search tab should be prefixed by an icon representing the new search engine - for each result.

reference_cases.title: TC-139
reference_cases.description:
INITIAL CONDITIONS
1. Open a new browser window.
2. All prefs should be set to their defaults (new profile).

STEPS/DESCRIPTION
1. Run the single-search test first.
2. Click the "Bookmark this Search" button below the search results.

EXPECTED RESULTS
1. A new bookmark folder titled "Search:(your query string here)". Should appear in the 4 Standard locations.
2. The "Bookmark this Search" button should not have become active until search results were generated.
